requirements.title: BTEST arguments are an integer and a valid bit position
requirements.definition: The I argument to BTEST shall be of type integer; POS shall be of type integer, nonnegative, and less than BIT_SIZE(I).

pending.btest-i-integer: Call BTEST with a nonnegative integer I such as 8; wrong-type I controls are unnumbered and expect no local diagnostic.
pending.btest-pos-integer: Call BTEST(8,3) with integer POS; wrong-type POS controls are unnumbered and expect no local diagnostic.
pending.btest-pos-nonnegative: Use the lower boundary POS=0 with BTEST(1,0) and assert .true. after initializing the result to .false.; negative POS remains an unnumbered program restriction with no local diagnostic facet. Mutate POS to 1 so the boundary assertion fails for value 1.
pending.btest-pos-less-than-bit-size: Set z=BIT_SIZE(0), assert z>0, then use the upper valid boundary POS=z-1 with BTEST(IBSET(0,z-1),z-1) asserted .true. and BTEST(0,z-1) asserted .false.; POS=z is an invalid program restriction but carries no local diagnostic facet here. Mutate POS to 0 in the IBSET/BTEST pair so the boundary bit rather than a low bit is load-bearing.

requirements.definition: The BTEST result is default logical.

pending.btest-result-default-logical: Initialize a default logical sentinel to .false., assign BTEST(8,3), and assert KIND(result)==KIND(.true.) plus the exact true value from the result-value facet.

requirements.title: BTEST reports whether bit POS of I is one
requirements.definition: BTEST returns true if bit POS of I has value 1 and false if bit POS of I has value 0, using the integer bit model of 16.3.

pending.btest-true-for-one-bit: Use result=.false. as a sentinel and assert BTEST(8,3) is true because bit position 3 of nonnegative integer 8 is one; mutate POS to 2 so the check fails.
pending.btest-false-for-zero-bit: Use result=.true. as a sentinel and assert BTEST(8,2) is false because bit position 2 of nonnegative integer 8 is zero; mutate POS to 3 so the check fails.
